text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and packet loss observed for inference fleet in us-west-2c (region us-west-2). Metric: inference-error-rate spiked to 11.8% over 5m, p95 latency -> 2400ms. Affected: g5-large pool (dedicated). Auto-remediation attempted: reattach load balancer target group, failed. Paging SRE oncall.

sre-oncall: I'm on it, looking at host health in us-west-2c. grabbing `kubectl --context prod-usw2c get pods -o wide` now.

infra-raj: I can see a spike in network retransmits on several nodes in subnet 10.2.48.0/20. Could be hypervisor network path degradation. Cloud provider dashboard shows elevated network path flaps in us-west-2c since ~15:12 UTC.

platform-tim: Noted. Routing checks: our cross-AZ NAT gateway metrics look normal but the instance RX misscount is high.

eng-ml-zoe: Customer impact: a handful of production customers (IDs: cust-821, cust-441) reported timeouts in chat/streaming flows. Auto-retries are resulting in duplicated embeddings and higher token cost.

devex-erin: Posting a quick customer-safe mitigation: increase client-side retry jitter and temporarily enable model-fallback to smaller-quantized model for requests routed to us-west-2c. Can we flip that flag?

ops-jen: @sre-oncall please run the canary routing policy to steer new sessions away from us-west-2c to us-west-2b and us-east-1 for critical customers. Command: `redwoodctl routes set-preference --region us-west-2c=0.1 --region us-west-2b=0.6 --region us-east-1=0.3 --scope production`

sre-oncall: Running that now. Patch applied at 15:22 UTC. Expect propagation ~30s. Will monitor error-rate and internal health.

incident-bot: ACTION: Route preference change applied by sre-oncall at 15:22:10 UTC.

infra-raj: I'm also kicking replacement instances in us-west-2c to see if warm hosts pick up traffic cleanly. `aws ec2 start-instances --instance-ids i-0bb...35 --region us-west-2` done.

eng-ml-zoe: Adding a request: for any in-flight sessions that drop, enable graceful reconnect window to avoid double billing tokens. Ops, can we extend session TTL to 45s?

platform-tim: Extended session reconnect TTL to 45s for affected route at 15:25 UTC.

devex-erin: Notifying customers in-app via status badge: "We observed increased latency for inference in us-west-2c; traffic is being shifted to healthy regions. No data loss expected."

customer-johnd: Thanks for the heads up — we saw about 20% of requests time out initially but retries helped. Please keep us posted on rollback window.

ops-jen: FYI, DNS TTL for regional endpoint was 60s. We lowered it to 15s at 15:26 UTC to accelerate client failover. `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://failover.json`

infra-raj: Cloud provider is acknowledging an AZ-level network fabric degradation; their internal ticket CN-9832 opened. They estimate stabilization in ~45-90 minutes but not committing. We'll keep steering traffic.

sre-oncall: Current numbers (15:30 UTC): error-rate down to 4.1% overall, us-west-2c still ~9% for remaining sticky sessions. p95 latency global down to 850ms. Continuing to drain instances in us-west-2c.

eng-ml-zoe: For customers on Dedicated pools in us-west-2c, we're offering to failover to Dedicated in us-west-2b or enable cross-region replication for stateful workloads. Ops, collect list of impacted dedicated pools.

ops-jen: Starting inventory: dedicated-pool-27, dedicated-pool-31 show increased errors. I'll open tickets to owners and start cross-region failover for pool-27.

devex-erin: Posting incident update to status.redwood.ai: "Mitigation in progress: traffic being shifted away from us-west-2c; partial customer impact. Engineering investigating AZ network degradation."

incident-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2029-usw2c-net-degrade. Sev: 2. Owner: sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: Handoff note for next oncall (starting 16:00 UTC): we have route preference applied, DNS TTL lowered, session TTL extended, replacement instances started. Remaining work: drain remaining sticky sessions in us-west-2c, confirm cloud provider stabilization, coordinate dedicated-pool failovers, customer comms. Leaving a brief runbook in PagerDuty.

ops-jen: I'll take handoff at 16:00 UTC and continue followups with cloud provider ticket CN-9832. If provider can't stabilize in 90m we'll execute cross-region bulk migration for impacted Dedicated pools.

customer-johnd: Appreciate the transparency. Will notify our SREs to avoid deploying during migration window.

eng-ml-zoe: Quick postmortem blurb to keep in thread later: root cause likely AZ network fabric congestion/flap leading to asymmetric routing and retransmits; secondary contributing factor: low DNS TTL previously which delayed some clients vs others.

sre-oncall: Marking this thread as active incident. Will update again in 30m or on any major changes.

ops-jen: (15:58 UTC) Update: provider reports partial mitigation, but some host NICs still show elevated drops. Continuing drain and cross-region steering.

sre-oncall: (16:05 UTC) Handing over to ops-jen. All oncall docs link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2029-usw2c-net-degrade

ops-jen: Taking over. Leaving note: if error-rate doesn't decline below 1% by 17:30 UTC initiate dedicated-pool bulk migration.

incident-bot: NOTE: This thread will be archived into INC-2029-usw2c-net-degrade once resolved.
